questions.stem: A particle $P$ of mass 0.4 kg is moving under the action of a constant force $\mathbf{F}$ newtons. Initially the velocity of $P$ is $(6\mathbf{i}-27\mathbf{j})$ m s$^{-1}$ and 4 s later the velocity of $P$ is $(-14\mathbf{i}+21\mathbf{j})$ m s$^{-1}$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find, in terms of $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$, the acceleration of $P$.
(3)

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
$|\mathbf{a}|=\sqrt{(5^2+12^2)}=13$ M1
$|\mathbf{F}|=m|\mathbf{a}|=0.4\times13=5.2$ N M1 A1
Alt: $\mathbf{F}=0.4(5\mathbf{i}+12\mathbf{j})=2\mathbf{i}+4.8\mathbf{j}$ M1
$|\mathbf{F}|=\sqrt{(2^2+4.8^2)}=5.2$ N M1 A1

questions.question_text:
A particle $P$ of mass 0.4 kg is moving under the action of a constant force $\mathbf{F}$ newtons. Initially the velocity of $P$ is $(6\mathbf{i}-27\mathbf{j})$ m s$^{-1}$ and 4 s later the velocity of $P$ is $(-14\mathbf{i}+21\mathbf{j})$ m s$^{-1}$.
(a) Find, in terms of $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$, the acceleration of $P$.
(3)
(b) Calculate the magnitude of $\mathbf{F}$.
(3)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
$\mathbf{a}=[-14\mathbf{i}+21\mathbf{j}-(6\mathbf{i}-27\mathbf{j})]\div 4$ M1 A1
$=(-5\mathbf{i}+12\mathbf{j})$ m s$^{-2}$ A1
$|\mathbf{a}|=\sqrt{(5^2+12^2)}=13$ M1
$|\mathbf{F}|=m|\mathbf{a}|=0.4\times13=5.2$ N M1 A1
Alt: $\mathbf{F}=0.4(5\mathbf{i}+12\mathbf{j})=2\mathbf{i}+4.8\mathbf{j}$ M1
$|\mathbf{F}|=\sqrt{(2^2+4.8^2)}=5.2$ N M1 A1

questions.stem: Two ships $P$ and $Q$ are moving along straight lines with constant velocities. Initially $P$ is at a point $O$ and the position vector of $Q$ relative to $O$ is $(6\mathbf{i}+12\mathbf{j})$ km, where $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are unit vectors directed due east and due north respectively. The ship $P$ is moving with velocity $10\mathbf{j}$ km h$^{-1}$ and $Q$ is moving with velocity $(-8\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j})$ km h$^{-1}$. At time $t$ hours the position vectors of $P$ and $Q$ relative to $O$ are $\mathbf{p}$ km and $\mathbf{q}$ km respectively.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Calculate the distance of $Q$ from $P$ when $t=3$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
$t=3$: $\mathbf{p}=30\mathbf{j}$, $\mathbf{q}=-18\mathbf{i}+30\mathbf{j}$ M1 A1
$\Rightarrow$ dist. apart $=18$ km A1
Alt: $\mathbf{PQ}=\mathbf{q}-\mathbf{p}=(6-8t)\mathbf{i}+(12-4t)\mathbf{j}$ M1
$t=3$: $\mathbf{PQ}=-18\mathbf{i}+0\mathbf{j}$ or $|\mathbf{PQ}|^2=(6-8t)^2+(12-4t)^2$ A1
Dist. $=18$ km, $t=3 \rightarrow |\mathbf{PQ}|=18$ A1

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Calculate the value of $t$ when $Q$ is due north of $P$.
(2)

questions.question_text:
Two ships $P$ and $Q$ are moving along straight lines with constant velocities. Initially $P$ is at a point $O$ and the position vector of $Q$ relative to $O$ is $(6\mathbf{i}+12\mathbf{j})$ km, where $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are unit vectors directed due east and due north respectively. The ship $P$ is moving with velocity $10\mathbf{j}$ km h$^{-1}$ and $Q$ is moving with velocity $(-8\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j})$ km h$^{-1}$. At time $t$ hours the position vectors of $P$ and $Q$ relative to $O$ are $\mathbf{p}$ km and $\mathbf{q}$ km respectively.
(a) Find $\mathbf{p}$ and $\mathbf{q}$ in terms of $t$.
(3)
(b) Calculate the distance of $Q$ from $P$ when $t=3$.
(3)
(c) Calculate the value of $t$ when $Q$ is due north of $P$.
(2)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
$\mathbf{p}=10t\mathbf{j}$ B1
$\mathbf{q}=(6\mathbf{i}+12\mathbf{j})+(-8\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j})t$ M1 A1
$t=3$: $\mathbf{p}=30\mathbf{j}$, $\mathbf{q}=-18\mathbf{i}+30\mathbf{j}$ M1 A1
$\Rightarrow$ dist. apart $=18$ km A1
Alt: $\mathbf{PQ}=\mathbf{q}-\mathbf{p}=(6-8t)\mathbf{i}+(12-4t)\mathbf{j}$ M1
$t=3$: $\mathbf{PQ}=-18\mathbf{i}+0\mathbf{j}$ or $|\mathbf{PQ}|^2=(6-8t)^2+(12-4t)^2$ A1
Dist. $=18$ km, $t=3 \rightarrow |\mathbf{PQ}|=18$ A1
$Q$ north of $P \Rightarrow 6-8t=0$ M1
$t=\frac{3}{4}$ A1

questions.stem:
Figure 1
A box of mass 1.5 kg is placed on a plane which is inclined at an angle of $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction between the box and plane is $\frac{1}{3}$. The box is kept in equilibrium by a light string which lies in a vertical plane containing a line of greatest slope of the plane. The string makes an angle of $20^\circ$ with the plane, as shown in Fig. 2. The box is in limiting equilibrium and is about to move up the plane. The tension in the string is $T$ newtons. The box is modelled as a particle.
Find the value of $T$.
(10)

parts.mark_scheme:
R($\nearrow$): $T\cos20^\circ=F+1.5g\sin30^\circ$ M1 A2,1,0

questions.stem:
Figure 3
A uniform rod $AB$ has length 3 m and weight 120 N. The rod rests in equilibrium in a horizontal position, smoothly supported at points $C$ and $D$, where $AC=0.5$ and $AD=2$ m, as shown in Fig. 3. A particle of weight $W$ newtons is attached to the rod at a point $E$ where $AE=x$ metres. The rod remains in equilibrium and the magnitude of the reaction at $C$ is now twice the magnitude of the reaction at $D$.

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
M($A$): $Wx+120\times1.5=R\times2+2R\times1$ M1 A2,1,0
R($\uparrow$) $3R=W+120$ M1 A1
Hence $Wx+180=3R=W=120$ M1
$W(1-x)=60$ A1
$W=\frac{60}{1-x}$ M1 A1cso

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Hence deduce the range of possible values of $x$.
(2)

questions.notes: [ms_verify] (a) '$Wx+180=3R=W+120$' -> '$Wx+180=3R=W=120$' (MS p.2: The official page prints '= W = 120', not '= W + 120'.)

A uniform rod $AB$ has length 3 m and weight 120 N. The rod rests in equilibrium in a horizontal position, smoothly supported at points $C$ and $D$, where $AC=0.5$ and $AD=2$ m, as shown in Fig. 3. A particle of weight $W$ newtons is attached to the rod at a point $E$ where $AE=x$ metres. The rod remains in equilibrium and the magnitude of the reaction at $C$ is now twice the magnitude of the reaction at $D$.
(a) Show that $W=\frac{60}{1-x}$.
(8)
(b) Hence deduce the range of possible values of $x$.

$W>0 \Rightarrow x<1$ M1 A1

questions.stem:
Figure 4
A particle $A$ of mass 0.8 kg rests on a horizontal table and is attached to one end of a light inextensible string. The string passes over a small smooth pulley $P$ fixed at the edge of the table. The other end of the string is attached to a particle $B$ of mass 1.2 kg which hangs freely below the pulley, as shown in Fig. 4. The system is released from rest with the string taut and with $B$ at a height of 0.6 m above the ground. In the subsequent motion $A$ does not reach $P$ before $B$ reaches the ground. In an initial model of the situation, the table is assumed to be smooth. Using this model, find

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) the tension in the string before $B$ reaches the ground,
(5)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) the time taken by $B$ to reach the ground.
(3)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
In a refinement of the model, it is assumed that the table is rough and that the coefficient of friction between $A$ and the table is $\frac{1}{5}$. Using this refined model,
(c) find the time taken by $B$ to reach the ground.
(8)
